mainTopic: שמיני עצרת as its own festival, שמחה on its night, ending the סוכה on the seventh day, and the start of ניסוך המים
overview: This amud opens by finishing a list from the previous daf. The list gives six ways that שמיני עצרת is a separate festival from סוכות, summed up by the memory sign פז"ר קש"ב. Next, a משנה teaches that הלל and שמחה last all eight days. The גמרא learns from the word "אך" in "והיית אך שמח" that the night of the last יום טוב is included in שמחה, because it follows a day of rejoicing. The first night is not included, because no day of rejoicing comes before it. A second משנה teaches that the סוכה must stay up all seven days, but the כלים may be moved into the house from מנחה onward. The גמרא then asks what someone does if he has no place to move his כלים. In ארץ ישראל he makes the סוכה invalid. In חוץ לארץ he lights a lamp in a small סוכה, or brings the cooking pots into a large one. Finally, a new משנה begins describing ניסוך המים: a golden jug filled from the שילוח, the שופר blasts at the שער המים, and the two basins on the מזבח. That description continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Six ways שמיני עצרת is its own festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a teaching from the previous daf. שמיני עצרת is a רגל בפני עצמו in six areas, remembered by the sign פז"ר קש"ב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a festival in its own right regarding פז"ר קש"ב: its own פייס, its own blessing of זמן, its own רגל, its own קרבן, its own שירה, and its own ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a statement that began on the previous daf. It lists six specific ways that שמיני עצרת is treated as a separate holiday, not just the eighth day of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פז"ר קש"ב is a memory sign made from six first letters: פייס, זמן, רגל, קרבן, שירה, ברכה. In each area, the eighth day starts fresh instead of continuing the pattern of סוכות. For example, there is a new פייס for the כהנים, a new שהחיינו, and a different number of קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: A festival in its own right, separate from the one before it
The lottery the כֹּהֲנִים used to decide who does each job in the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
The blessing of שֶׁהֶחֱיָנוּ, said at the start of a festival
The offerings brought that day
The songs the לְוִיִּם sang while the offerings were brought
The holiday wording added to תְּפִלָּה and בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן

steps.confusionAlert: The word רגל appears twice here. The first time, it is the general heading: שמיני עצרת is a separate festival. The second time, it is one specific item on the list. Per many מפרשים, it refers to the fact that there is no מצוה of סוכה on this day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why we say שהחיינו on שמיני עצרת. It also explains why our תפלה mentions "שמיני חג העצרת" and not סוכות.

phrases.english: It is a festival in its own right
regarding PaZeR KeSheV (a memory sign).
phrases.notes: An acronym made of the six items that follow.

phrases.english: Its own lottery.
phrases.notes: A new lottery is held for the כהנים.

phrases.english: Its own 'time' blessing.
Its own festival.
phrases.notes: For example, there is no סוכה obligation.

phrases.english: Its own offering.
phrases.notes: Its offerings are a new count, not a continuation of the סוכות count.

phrases.english: Its own song.
Its own blessing.
phrases.notes: It has its own holiday wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ לְעִנְיַן פָּזֵ״‎ר קֶשֶׁ״‎ב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement about שמיני עצרת that began on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמיני עצרת is a separate festival with respect to פייס, זמן, רגל, קרבן, שירה, and ברכה.

steps.title: The משנה: הלל and rejoicing all eight days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that הלל and שמחה apply for all eight days. A person must treat the last יום טוב with the same הלל, שמחה, and honor as the rest of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: הלל and rejoicing are for eight days. How so? This teaches that a person is obligated in הלל, in rejoicing, and in honoring the last יום טוב of the חג, just like all the other days of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that even though שמיני עצרת is its own holiday, the obligations of הלל and שמחה still apply on it, just as on the days of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some מצוות of סוכות, like סוכה and לולב, stop after seven days. The משנה tells us that הלל and שמחה are different: they continue through the eighth day. Here, שמחה means eating the meat of שלמים, the peace-offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'
The special chapters of praise from תְּהִלִּים said on festivals
The מצוה to rejoice on the festival, mainly by eating שְׁלָמִים
Honoring the holiday, for example with special clothing and food
How so? This introduces an explanation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this contradicts Step 1. שמיני עצרת is a separate festival, but a separate festival can still carry these same obligations.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
הלל and rejoicing are for eight days.
How so?
This teaches that a person is obligated
in הלל and in rejoicing

phrases.aramaic: וּבִכְבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג
phrases.english: and in honoring the last יום טוב of the festival
just like all the other days of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It expands on the first משנה of the perek.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an obligation of הלל, שמחה, and כבוד יום טוב on שמיני עצרת, just as on the other days of the חג.

steps.title: Where do we learn this from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the eighth day has a מצוה of שמחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source in the פסוקים. This is a setup line: the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is focused on שמחה on the eighth day. We might not assume it, because the תורה speaks of seven days of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא, the discussion of the משנה
From where do we know these things? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the obligation of שמחה on the last יום טוב.

steps.title: The verse 'והיית אך שמח' includes the last night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "והיית אך שמח" that the night of the last יום טוב is included in the מצוה of שמחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'And you shall be only joyful.' This comes to include the nights of the last יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The extra words in the פסוק teach that you must rejoice even on the night of שמיני עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night you cannot bring a new קרבן. So שמחה that night means eating שלמים that were brought earlier, during the day. The ברייתא reads the פסוק as extending שמחה to that night.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall be only joyful' (דברים טז:טו)
To include something extra
The nights of

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'And you shall be only joyful'
comes to include the nights of the last יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "והיית אך שמח" includes the night of the last יום טוב in שמחה.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the first night instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: maybe the extra night that the פסוק adds is the first night of יום טוב, not the last.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is only the first יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading. It suggests the פסוק could be adding the first night of סוכות instead of the night of שמיני עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On both nights, rejoicing would have to come from שלמים brought on an earlier day, because קרבנות are not brought at night. So the פסוק's extra inclusion could seemingly point to either night.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only. This proposes another reading
The first יום טוב of סוכות

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן?
phrases.english: Or perhaps it means only the first יום טוב?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק includes the last night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could just as easily be adding the first night.

steps.title: The word 'אך' divides
steps.stepSummary: The word "אך" limits the inclusion. It tells us that only one of the two nights is included, not both.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'only' (אך), it divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that "אך" is a word that limits. It splits the two nights so that one is included and one is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without "אך" we might include both nights. "אך" cuts that down to just one. The next step asks which night is the included one, and Step 8 answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Only. A limiting word (מִיעוּט)
It divided, meaning it made a distinction

steps.confusionAlert: "אך" does not by itself tell us which night is included. It only tells us that the two nights are treated differently. The reasoning in Step 8 is what decides which one.

phrases.english: When it says 'only'
it made a distinction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by pointing to the limiting word "אך".
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "אך" divides, so only one of the two nights is included.

steps.title: Why include the last night and not the first?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason we have to include the last night and leave out the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to include the nights of the last יום טוב and exclude the nights of the first יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: Since "אך" only says that one night is included, the ברייתא asks how we know it is the last night. This sets up the reasoning in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question needs a logical reason, because the פסוק itself does not say which night it means.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? This asks for the reasoning behind a choice
To exclude

phrases.english: And what did you see
to include the nights of the last יום טוב
and exclude the nights of the first יום טוב?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the idea that "אך" divides by asking which night is included.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the last night is included rather than the first.

steps.title: The last night follows a day of rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: The last night is included because a day of שמחה comes before it. The first night is excluded because no day of שמחה comes before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the nights of the last יום טוב, because there is rejoicing before it. I exclude the nights of the first יום טוב, because there is no rejoicing before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its reason. The last night continues the rejoicing of the day before, while the first night has nothing before it to continue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the seventh day, people brought שלמים, and that meat can still be eaten on the eighth night. That makes it natural for the שמחה to continue. ערב סוכות is not a day of שמחה, so there is no such continuation into the first night.

keyTerms.meaning: I include
Because there is rejoicing before it
I exclude

steps.whatToRemember: The night of שמיני עצרת has a מצוה of שמחה, learned from "והיית אך שמח". "אך" limits the inclusion to one night. We pick the last night because it follows a day of rejoicing, while the first night does not.

phrases.aramaic: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן —
phrases.english: I include the nights of the last יום טוב,
since there is rejoicing before it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹצִיא אֲנִי לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: and I exclude the nights of the first יום טוב,
since there is no rejoicing before it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the last night is chosen.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The last night follows a day of שמחה, so the rejoicing continues into it. The first night has no such day before it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מצוה of שמחה includes the night of שמיני עצרת but not the first night of סוכות.

steps.title: The סוכה lasts all seven days, but the כלים come down from מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may not take down his סוכה after his last meal on the seventh day, but from מנחה onward he may move his כלים into the house to honor the last יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The סוכה is for seven days. How so? Once he finishes eating on the seventh day, he should not take apart his סוכה. But he may take the כלים down from the time of מנחה and later, out of respect for the last יום טוב of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the מצוה of סוכה lasts the whole seventh day, but late in that day a person may start moving his things back into the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finishing the last meal does not end the מצוה, because the obligation lasts until the end of the seventh day. So the סוכה must stay standing. Moving the כלים from מנחה onward is allowed because the house needs to be ready for שמיני עצרת, which is a separate יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
He should not take apart
He takes the כלים down (into the house)
From the time of מנחה and later
The last יום טוב of the חג, meaning שמיני עצרת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that finishing the last meal means you are done with the סוכה. The מצוה lasts until the end of the seventh day. Moving the כלים is only a preparation for the coming יום טוב.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The sukka is for seven days.
How so?

phrases.aramaic: גָּמַר מִלֶּאֱכוֹל — לֹא יַתִּיר אֶת סוּכָּתוֹ.
phrases.english: If he finished eating, he should not take apart his sukka.
But he takes down the vessels
phrases.notes: He moves them from the סוכה into the house.

phrases.english: from minḥa time and onward,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: out of respect for the last Yom Tov of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It moves on from the שמחה discussion to the rules for ending the סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוכה stays standing all of the seventh day. The כלים may be moved into the house from מנחה onward to honor שמיני עצרת.

steps.title: What if he has no כלים to take down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a person should do if he has no כלים to take down.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If he has no כלים to take down, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the משנה. It asks what happens if a person has no כלים to move out of the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses moving the כלים as the sign that the סוכה time is ending. So the גמרא asks how this works for someone who has nothing to move. This first wording of the question will be challenged right away.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
He does not have
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אֵין לוֹ כֵּלִים לְהוֹרִיד, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: GEMARA: If he has no vessels to take down, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case the משנה does not cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a person does at the end of the seventh day if he has no כלים to move.

steps.title: Everyone used some כלים in the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the question: it is impossible to have no כלים, since he must have eaten with something all week.
steps.simpleTranslation: He has no כלים?! When he used the סוכה, what did he use?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own question. It says the case cannot happen, because anyone who ate in the סוכה used dishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on how the case was set up, not on any law. Eating in the סוכה all week means using כלים, so there are always כלים to take down. The question has to be asked differently.

keyTerms.meaning: He used
With what?

phrases.english: He has no vessels?!
But when he used the sukka, with what did he use it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לוֹ כֵּלִים?! אֶלָּא כִּי אִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ בְּמַאי אִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way step 10 set up the case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case in step 10 of someone who has no כלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anyone who ate in the סוכה used כלים, so the case cannot exist.

steps.title: The real question: he has no place to put his כלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the question: what if he has no place to move his כלים, so he must keep eating in the סוכה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is: if he has no place to take down his כלים, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the question. The person has כלים but no other place to eat, so he will keep eating in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the problem is clear. If he keeps eating in the סוכה on שמיני עצרת, it can look as if he is adding to the מצוה, which is בל תוסיף. The question is how he can show that he is now eating there only because he has no choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the question must be reworded)
He has no place
The prohibition against adding to a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: The words בל תוסיף do not appear in this text. They are the reason behind the question, as the commentaries explain: eating in the סוכה on the eighth day can look like adding to the מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לְהוֹרִיד כֵּלָיו, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Rather: if he has no place to take down his vessels, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לְהוֹרִיד כֵּלָיו, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rewords the question of step 10 after the challenge in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How someone who must keep eating in the סוכה shows that he is not adding to the מצוה.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר רב: make a four-טפחים gap in the סכך
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר רב says he opens a gap of four טפחים in the סכך, which makes the סוכה invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר רב said: He opens a gap of four טפחים in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: he makes the סוכה invalid by opening a four-טפחים gap in the סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the סוכה is invalid, eating in it cannot count as the מצוה. Everyone can see that he is just eating in a convenient spot, so there is no adding to the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: He opens a gap in, he reduces
Four (טפחים), enough to make the סוכה invalid

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav said:
He opens a gap of four handbreadths in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר (רַב) אָמַר: פּוֹחֵת בָּהּ אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He makes the סוכה invalid with a four-טפחים gap.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: light a lamp in the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says he lights a lamp inside the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: He lights a lamp in it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: he does not make the סוכה invalid. Instead he lights a lamp inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally people do not light a lamp in a סוכה, because of the risk of fire. Lighting one is a clear change that shows this is no longer the מצוה סוכה. At first glance this looks like a disagreement with רבי חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He lights
Lamp

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
He lights a lamp in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: מַדְלִיק בָּהּ אֶת הַנֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He lights a lamp in the סוכה to mark that it is no longer used for the מצוה.

steps.title: No disagreement: one answer is for חוץ לארץ, one for ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two אמוראים do not disagree. Each answer fits a different place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree: this one is for us, and this one is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two answers are not really an argument. Each one is for a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל the eighth day is surely not סוכות, so they may make the סוכה invalid (רבי חייא בר רב). In חוץ לארץ the eighth day might be the seventh, because of the doubt about the date. They still need a valid סוכה, so they cannot ruin it and light a lamp instead (רבי יהושע בן לוי).

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
This is for us (בבל), and this is for them (ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this is for us, and this is for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי: הָא לַן וְהָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent argument between steps 13 and 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different places (ארץ ישראל versus חוץ לארץ)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two אמוראים argue about what to do.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ארץ ישראל he makes the סוכה invalid. In חוץ לארץ, where the סוכה is still needed because of the doubt, he lights a lamp.

steps.title: A lamp works for a small סוכה, but what about a large one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lamp answer: it only works in a small סוכה. What does someone with a large סוכה do?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for a small סוכה. But for a large סוכה, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a gap in the lamp answer. In a large סוכה, lighting a lamp does not show any change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a small סוכה people avoid lamps because of fire danger, so a lamp stands out. In a large סוכה lamps are normal, so lighting one sends no message. Someone in חוץ לארץ with a large סוכה still needs a way to show the change.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well for
A small סוכה
What can be said?

phrases.english: This works well for a small sukka,
but for a large sukka, what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תִּינַח סוּכָּה קְטַנָּה, סוּכָּה גְּדוֹלָה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lamp answer from step 14, as it was applied in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's lamp answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lamp only shows a change where lamps are normally avoided. In a large סוכה lamps are normal.

steps.title: In a large סוכה, bring the cooking pots inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in a large סוכה he brings his cooking pots inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings eating כלים into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different sign for a large סוכה: he brings in his cooking pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pots are normally kept out of the סוכה. Bringing them in is an unusual change that shows the סוכה is no longer being used for the מצוה. The next step brings the source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings in
Eating כלים, such as pots and pans

phrases.english: That he brings eating vessels into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different sign that fits a large סוכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A large סוכה has no way to show the change.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bringing the pots inside shows the change.

steps.title: רבא: pots stay outside the סוכה, drinking cups stay inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the answer with רבא's rule that eating כלים belong outside the סוכה and drinking כלים inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: Eating כלים go outside the סוכה. Drinking כלים go inside the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's rule to explain why bringing pots in shows a change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally pots are kept out of the סוכה, but cups may stay inside. So bringing pots in breaks the normal pattern. That makes the סוכה look like it is no longer a מצוה סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The סוכה (Aramaic)
Outside of
Drinking כלים, such as cups

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה requires the סוכה all seven days, with the כלים moved inside from מנחה. Someone who must keep eating in it on the eighth day shows the change. In ארץ ישראל he makes the סכך invalid. In חוץ לארץ he lights a lamp in a small סוכה, or brings the pots into a large one.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
Eating vessels go outside the sukka.
Drinking vessels go in the sukka.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא: מָאנֵי מֵיכְלָא — בַּר מִמְּטַלַּלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the answer of step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That bringing pots into the סוכה is an unusual change
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's rule that eating כלים go outside the סוכה and drinking כלים inside

steps.title: How the water libation was done: filling the golden jug
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה asks how נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם was done. It answers that a golden jug holding three לוגין was filled from the שילוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How was the water libation done? A golden jug that held three לוגין was filled with water from the שילוח spring.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה opens. It asks how the water libation worked and starts the answer with the first stage: filling the jug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כיצד is not a challenge. It is the משנה's way of saying 'here is how it was done.' The first details are the jug (gold), its size (three לוגין), and where the water came from (the שילוח).

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין. It marks the start of the משנה text
The water libation. Water was poured on the מזבח on סוכות
A jug or flask
A measure of volume. The jug held three of them
The Siloam spring or pool near Jerusalem

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read כיצד as a קשיא. Nobody is attacking anything here. The משנה is simply opening a description of the procedure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the main source for how the water libation was done. The whole סוגיא that follows builds on these details.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Marks a new משנה. The previous גמרא discussion is over.

phrases.english: The water libation, how was it done?
phrases.notes: An opening question that introduces a description. It is not a challenge.

phrases.english: A jug of gold
holding three log
he would fill from the Siloam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is separate from the previous גמרא discussion about the סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water for the libation was drawn from the שילוח in a golden jug holding three לוגין.

steps.title: שופר blasts at the שער המים
steps.stepSummary: When they reached the שער המים, they blew תקיעה, תרועה, and תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they reached the Water Gate, they blew a תקיעה, a תרועה, and another תקיעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the procedure. When the group carrying the water reaches the שער המים, the שופר is blown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds the second stage, arriving at the עזרה through a specific gate. The gate is called the שער המים because this water was carried in through it. The blasts follow the standard pattern of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, and they show the joy of the occasion.

keyTerms.meaning: The Water Gate, a gate of the עזרה
They blew a תקיעה, one long blast
They blew a תרועה, a broken or wavering blast

phrases.english: They reached the Water Gate,
they sounded a tekia, a terua, and a tekia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next stage of the same procedure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shofar blasts of תקיעה, תרועה, and תקיעה were sounded at the שער המים.

steps.title: Going up the ramp to the two silver basins
steps.stepSummary: The כהן goes up the כבש, turns left, and finds two silver basins there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went up the ramp of the מזבח and turned to his left. Two silver basins were there.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה follows the כהן to the מזבח. It tells us where the basins were and what they were made of, according to the first, unnamed opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The location is exact: up the כבש, then a turn to the left. There he finds two basins that the water will be poured into. The claim that they were silver is the view of the תנא קמא, and רבי יהודה challenges it next.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Basins or bowls
Silver

phrases.english: He ascended the ramp
and turned to his left,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי סְפָלִים שֶׁל כֶּסֶף הָיוּ שָׁם.
phrases.english: two silver basins were there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the procedure, now at the מזבח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were two silver basins to the left at the top of the כבש.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the basins were limestone, darkened by wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees about what the basins were made of. He says they were limestone, and they only looked like silver because the wine had darkened them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: they were made of limestone. But their surfaces had turned dark because of the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion appears inside the משנה. רבי יהודה argues about the material of the basins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said silver. רבי יהודה says limestone. He also explains why people might think they were silver: the wine poured into them darkened the stone, so it looked like tarnished silver. Both opinions agree there were two basins. The only argument is about the material.

keyTerms.meaning: Limestone or plaster
Darkened or blackened
Wine. The wine libation was also poured into these basins

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not deny that there were two basins. He only disputes what they were made of.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
they were of limestone,
but their surfaces had become blackened
because of the wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר שֶׁל סִיד הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא about the basins' material
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the basins were limestone that looked like silver because the wine darkened them.

steps.title: The basins had holes in them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה goes back to the shared description and begins explaining that the basins were perforated. The text continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they were perforated...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה leaves רבי יהודה's side point and returns to describing the basins. This word begins the next detail, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holes let the water and wine drain out of the basins and down through the מזבח into the שיתין, the channels beneath it. The משנה will next explain the size of the holes.

keyTerms.meaning: Perforated, having holes

phrases.english: and perforated
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the description of the holes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבי יהודה's view to the shared description of the basins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The basins had holes so their contents could flow down through the מזבח into the שיתין.
